fixtureScope: Published identity/prose projection for six exact model-years plus incompatible XT6/Kicks negatives; commerce tested separately

rows.title: Auto Idle-Stop Failure to Restart (2016-2020 MDX)
rows.description: On 2016-2020 Acura MDX with the 3.5L V6 (J35Y5) and Auto Idle-Stop, the engine may fail to automatically restart from a stop event, leaving the driver stranded in traffic. NHTSA opened an Engineering Analysis (PE22-016 → EA) after 1,300+ complaints across ~2.2M Honda/Acura vehicles, with 4 confirmed accidents. Acura issued Service Bulletin 23-001 in January 2023 with a PGM-FI software update (reduces idle-stop operating range) and extended warranty coverage on starter replacement and valve adjustment to 10 years / unlimited miles. Note: the Sport Hybrid (J30Y1) uses a different motor-based stop/start system and is not in scope of this TSB.
rows.solution: Have dealer perform the PGM-FI idle-stop software update plus starter / starter relay inspection per Honda's 2023 service campaign (covered 10 years). To avoid recurrence, defeat Idle-Stop with the dash button each drive or install an aftermarket auto-disable module.

rows.title: Fuel Pump Impeller Deformation Causing Stall (NHTSA Recall 23V-858)
rows.description: Certain 2018-2020 MDX (J35Y5 3.5L V6) and MDX Sport Hybrid (3.0L V6 hybrid) units were built with low-density, improperly molded in-tank fuel pump impellers. Surface cracking from production solvent absorption causes the impeller to swell and seize against the pump body, leading to no-start or stall while driving. Honda issued NHTSA recall 23V-858 covering ~2.5 million Honda/Acura vehicles.
rows.solution: Free recall remedy under NHTSA 23V-858 - dealer replaces the fuel pump module with a redesigned part. Check VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls or owners.acura.com and schedule replacement immediately if not yet completed.

rows.title: Infotainment System Random Reboots
rows.description: The AcuraLink infotainment system in third-gen MDX models experiences random reboots during driving, temporarily disabling navigation, audio, and the backup camera. The system takes 30-60 seconds to restart, leaving the driver without audio or navigation guidance mid-route.
rows.solution: Update to the latest infotainment firmware from an Acura dealer. Reset the system to factory defaults and clear cached data. If reboots continue, the infotainment control module may need hardware replacement under an extended warranty program.

rows.title: ZF 9-Speed Automatic Transmission Shudder and Harsh Shifting
rows.description: Third-generation MDX models with the ZF 9-speed automatic suffer from torque converter shudder during light throttle acceleration between 30-50 mph. The lockup clutch in the torque converter vibrates as it engages, creating a sensation similar to driving over rumble strips that many owners mistake for an engine misfire.
rows.solution: Update the TCM software to the latest Acura calibration that modifies torque converter lockup strategy. Perform a complete ATF drain and refill with Honda DW-1. If shudder persists after software update and fluid change, the torque converter assembly must be replaced.

rows.title: ZF 9-Speed Transmission Hesitation, Hard Shifts and Stalling (2016-2019 MDX)
rows.description: The ZF 9HP 9-speed automatic introduced on the 2016 MDX suffers from documented hesitation, harsh shifts, lurching, and unexpected downshifts/deceleration. Drivers report the vehicle hesitating from a stop, banging into gear, or briefly losing power. Software miscommunication between TCM, ECM and throttle control is the alleged root cause; a class action was filed alleging Honda knew of the defect from 2015.
rows.solution: Have dealer apply latest TCM/PGM-FI software updates first (covered by powertrain warranty). If symptoms persist, request fluid replacement and dealer escalation; document everything for lemon-law/class-action relief. Avoid jerky throttle inputs while cold.

rows.title: 2020 XT6 Start/Stop Accumulator May Be Missing Endcap Bolts — Recall 20V668000
rows.description: Only the 2020 model year of the Cadillac XT6 falls inside this GM recall, which addresses a start/stop transmission accumulator that may have left the plant with bolts missing from its endcap. Because those bolts hold the endcap against transmission oil pressure, the missing hardware can allow a transmission oil leak. NHTSA's consequence statement is blunt about where that goes: the leak may progress to a loss of propulsion, increasing crash risk, and transmission fluid in the presence of an ignition source may increase the risk of fire. The same defect was found across a range of 2018-2020 Chevrolet, Buick, GMC and Cadillac vehicles; the XT6's exposure is the 2020 year alone.
rows.solution: Free of charge at a Cadillac dealer: the technician inspects the start/stop transmission accumulator on your 2020 XT6 and replaces the unit if any endcap bolts are missing. The recall opened to owners on December 15, 2020. If you bought the XT6 used, do not assume the previous owner had it done — check the VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls, then book the inspection through Cadillac customer service at 1-800-458-8006. GM's recall number is N202313440.

rows.title: 2021 XT6 Fuel Supply Line May Separate and Leak — Recall 21V422
rows.description: If you own a 2021 Cadillac XT6, this one is worth a VIN check. GM recalled a limited group of 2021 XT6, XT5 and GMC Acadia vehicles because the fuel supply lines may have been improperly attached and seated at the factory. NHTSA's consequence statement is blunt: lines that are not properly seated may loosen or separate, causing a fuel leak, which increases the risk of a fire. The whole campaign covers 572 vehicles across all of the models listed, so inclusion is the exception rather than the rule for the XT6 — but the potential outcome is serious enough that verifying by VIN is the right move rather than waiting to notice a problem. GM's internal recall number is N212335590, and owner letters were mailed July 1, 2021.
rows.solution: Free of charge at a Cadillac dealer: the technician inspects the fuel supply lines and replaces them as necessary so they are correctly attached and seated. Enter your XT6's VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls to see whether this campaign applies to your specific vehicle, since the affected population is small. If it does apply and you notice a fuel odor or any sign of leaking fuel in the meantime, stop driving the vehicle and have it towed in. Cadillac customer service: 1-800-458-8006, GM recall number N212335590.

rows.title: 2022 XT6 Left-Rear Toe Link May Be Loose or Separate — Recall 22V427
rows.description: If you drive a 2022 Cadillac XT6, check this one. General Motors recalled a group of these SUVs after finding that the left-rear suspension toe link may not have been tightened properly. An under-tightened fastener can allow the toe link to go loose over time, and a loose toe link can separate outright. GM's stated consequence is blunt: separation can cause a loss of vehicle control and increases the risk of a crash. NHTSA logged the campaign as 22V427000 in the SUSPENSION:REAR component group; GM's own number for it is N222364330. The 2022 Cadillac XT5 and 2022 GMC Acadia are covered by the same campaign. NHTSA's record does not state how many vehicles were affected campaign-wide.
rows.solution: The fix costs the owner nothing. A Cadillac dealer inspects the left-rear suspension and replaces the fastener if it turns out to be loose or missing. Notification letters went out to owners on July 11, 2022, so if you bought the vehicle used you may never have seen one — enter your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls to see whether your XT6 is on the list and whether the repair is still open. Cadillac customer service is 1-800-458-8006, recall N222364330.

rows.title: 3.6L LGX Engine Oil Migrating Into the Cooling System Through Block Porosity — Overheating with Sludge in the Radiator
rows.description: GM bulletin 21-NA-108 (which superseded PIP5257E) covers engine overheating with the cooling system contaminated by engine oil, and it lists the 2020-2021 Cadillac XT6 with the 3.6L LGX V6 among the affected applications. The failure is not a head gasket in the usual sense: pressurized oil from the main oil gallery migrates into a coolant water jacket through porosity or a thin-wall casting defect in the engine block. Because oil pressure is far higher than coolant pressure, oil pushes into the coolant rather than the other way round, and the surge tank and radiator fill with a thick brown oil-and-coolant emulsion that looks like a milkshake. That emulsion will not carry heat, so the engine overheats, and it plugs the radiator and heater core. GM bulletins 21-NA-147 and 22-NA-240 cover the related diagnosis of a coolant and/or oil leak with the malfunction indicator lamp on. This is engine-code specific — it is an LGX 3.6L casting issue and is not a claim about the 2.0L LSY turbo four also sold in the XT6.
rows.solution: Do not just flush the coolant and refill — the contamination will come straight back. Follow the bulletin's diagnostic sequence, which confirms the source by pressure-testing and by checking whether the oil level drops while the coolant turns to emulsion. Where the leak path is traced to block porosity, the repair is an engine block or complete engine replacement, which is why this is worth pursuing under the 6-year/70,000-mile GM powertrain warranty while it is still in force; document the concern in writing at the first sign of contamination. If contamination is confirmed, the radiator, surge tank, heater core and oil cooler all need flushing or replacement, since emulsified oil coats every passage. Out of warranty an engine replacement on an XT6 typically runs $8,000-$12,000.

rows.title: Low-Speed TCC Shudder Must Be Confirmed Before a Fluid Drain and Fill
rows.description: GM PIP5608F covers 2020-2021 XT6 vehicles with 9-speed transmissions RPO M3G or M3W when torque-converter clutch shudder occurs on re-apply after a shift at 40 mph or below. GM identifies possible excessive assembly lubricant in the fluid and requires confirmation with TCC slip data or the scan-tool command test.
rows.solution: Have a qualified transmission technician verify RPO M3G or M3W and confirm the event is TCC shudder using slip-speed data or the commanded-on test. If the bulletin criteria are met, follow the GM DEXRON VI drain-and-fill procedure and drive at least 200 miles before judging the repair. Do not use a universal additive or flush kit. The exact ShowMeTheParts lookup returned no transmission-fluid candidate.

rows.title: Auto Start-Stop Harshness and Battery Issues
rows.description: The auto start-stop system engages and disengages harshly, causing the vehicle to shudder on restart. The AGM battery required for the system degrades quickly, and when it weakens, the start-stop system becomes erratic or disables itself. Many owners find the system intrusive.
rows.solution: Replace the AGM battery with a fresh ACDelco unit if the system is not functioning properly. Have the battery monitor sensor reset after replacement. GM has released recalibrations to improve start-stop smoothness. Aftermarket start-stop eliminator modules are available for owners who want to permanently disable the feature.

rows.title: Electric Power Steering Rack Failure — "Steering Assist Is Reduced / Service Power Steering" with C0460 or C0545
rows.description: XT6 owners report a "Steering Assist is Reduced — Drive with Care" or "Service Power Steering" message in the driver information center, usually with a noticeable increase in steering effort. GM bulletin 20-NA-215 covers this condition on the XT5 and XT6 and ties it to DTCs C0460 and/or C0545 stored in the power steering module. The XT6 uses a belt-drive electric rack with the motor and control module integrated into the steering gear, so an internal fault or a torque-sensor signal fault sets the code and the module deliberately cuts or reduces assist rather than allowing erratic assist. Steering is still mechanically connected — the car remains steerable — but effort rises sharply, which is most alarming at parking-lot speeds or in an evasive maneuver. Owners also describe a separate, milder version where assist fades after sustained low-speed maneuvering and returns once the system cools; that thermal derate is normal protection, not a failed rack, and it clears itself.
rows.solution: Have the power steering module scanned first. A stored C0460 or C0545 per bulletin 20-NA-215 calls for replacement of the complete steering gear assembly — the module is not serviced separately. After the rack is replaced the steering angle sensor must be recalibrated with a capable scan tool or the system will not function and the message will return. Out of warranty a rack and calibration typically runs roughly $1,500-$2,600 at a dealer. Before replacing anything, rule out the thermal derate (assist returns after cooling, no stored code) and a weak battery or poor ground, either of which can trigger a false assist-reduced message on this platform. The XT6's powertrain warranty does not cover this, but the 4-year/50,000-mile bumper-to-bumper coverage does.

rows.title: Incorrect Transmission Sun Gear Lets the Driver-Side Half-Shaft Disengage — Recall 23V172
rows.description: NHTSA campaign 23V172000 (GM safety recall N222389310) covers 613 model-year 2023 Cadillac XT6 vehicles built with an incorrect sun gear inside the transmission's final drive. The wrong gear does not retain the driver-side (left front) half-shaft correctly, and the shaft can disengage from the transmission. Two failure modes follow: while driving, the wheel stops receiving torque and the vehicle loses drive power; while parked, the park pawl can no longer hold the vehicle through a disengaged shaft, so the XT6 can roll away even with the shifter in Park. The same wrong-gear condition was recalled on the Cadillac XT5, Chevrolet Blazer and Traverse, and GMC Acadia, but confirm your own VIN rather than assuming a sibling's campaign applies.
rows.solution: A free recall remedy exists. Dealers replace the sun gears at no charge under NHTSA 23V172000 / GM N222389310; owner letters were mailed May 1, 2023. Until the repair is done, always set the parking brake when parking. If drive power has already been lost, have the vehicle towed rather than driven — a fully disengaged half-shaft will not propel the car and can damage the transmission case.

rows.title: Instrument Panel Fails to Illuminate Hazard, High-Beam and Turn-Signal Telltales — Software Recall 24V459
rows.description: NHTSA campaign 24V459000 covers late-build Cadillac XT6 vehicles on which the instrument panel cluster may not illuminate when the hazard warning lights, high beams, or turn signals are activated. The cluster software fails to light the corresponding telltales, so the driver gets no confirmation that the hazards are flashing, that the high beams are on, or that a turn signal is active. The exterior lamps themselves still work — the failure is the driver's feedback. That matters because a driver who cannot see the high-beam indicator may leave the brights on and blind oncoming traffic, and a driver who cannot see the turn-signal telltale may leave a signal running or believe the hazards are off when the vehicle is stopped on a shoulder. This is a software defect in the instrument cluster, not a bulb or wiring failure.
rows.solution: A free recall remedy exists and it is purely a reflash. Dealers update the instrument panel cluster software at no charge under NHTSA 24V459000; owner letters were expected August 5, 2024. If your XT6 exhibits the symptom, check the VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls before paying anyone to diagnose a cluster — replacing the cluster is not the fix and is not necessary.

rows.title: Loss of Cabin Heat Caused by an Engine Control Module Software Anomaly — Bulletin 22-NA-094
rows.description: GM bulletin 22-NA-094, issued July 2022, addresses a loss of cabin heat on the Cadillac XT6 and XT5. Owners get little or no warm air from the vents even after the engine reaches operating temperature — the complaint typically shows up in cold weather and is easy to misdiagnose as a stuck thermostat, an air pocket in the cooling system, a blend door actuator, or a plugged heater core. GM traced it instead to a software anomaly in the engine control module: the ECM's thermal management strategy does not bring coolant temperature up or route flow to the heater core as intended, so the heater has nothing hot to work with. Because the fault is calibration rather than hardware, no part is actually broken, and owners who let a shop chase it mechanically can spend hundreds of dollars replacing a perfectly good thermostat or heater core before the real fix is applied.
rows.solution: The fix is a reprogram, not a part. Per bulletin 22-NA-094, the correction is to reprogram the engine control module with the updated calibration; this is a dealer or capable-shop operation using GM's programming tools and takes about an hour. Ask specifically for bulletin 22-NA-094 by number. Before authorizing a thermostat or heater core replacement for a no-heat complaint on an XT6, confirm the ECM calibration is current — under the 4-year/50,000-mile bumper-to-bumper warranty the reprogram is free, and even out of warranty it typically runs $100-$200 against $600-$1,400 for a heater core job that would not have fixed it.

rows.title: AWD Power Transfer Unit Fluid Leak
rows.description: The Power Transfer Unit (PTU) on AWD-equipped XT6 models develops seal leaks that allow fluid to seep out. Low PTU fluid causes the internal gears and bearings to wear prematurely, eventually producing a whining noise. The PTU is not included in routine maintenance schedules, so leaks often go unnoticed.
rows.solution: Inspect the PTU seals and replace if leaking. Top off with the GM-specified PTU fluid. If the PTU is already noisy from running low on fluid, replacement is required as the unit is not rebuildable. Add PTU fluid level check to your routine maintenance schedule every 15,000 miles.

rows.title: Rearview Camera Cuts Out Due to Bad Coaxial Cable Crimp on Surround Vision-Equipped XT6 (Recall 22V709000)
rows.description: If your 2020 or 2021 Cadillac XT6 was ordered with the optional Surround Vision feature, it may be part of NHTSA recall 22V709000. GM found that the coaxial cable connectors carrying the rearview camera signal may have been crimped improperly, and a faulty crimp can cause the rearview camera to fail outright or work only intermittently. The practical effect for an XT6 driver is a missing or unreliable rear image when reversing, which NHTSA notes reduces rear visibility and increases crash risk. XT6s without Surround Vision are not covered. The campaign as a whole spans 95,231 vehicles across all the models it includes - that number is for the entire campaign and says nothing about how many XT6s are involved. GM tracks the recall internally as N222378380 and mailed owner letters on January 18, 2023.
rows.solution: Dealers replace the affected coaxial cables at no charge to the owner. Take the XT6 to any Cadillac dealer and ask them to perform recall N222378380 / NHTSA 22V709000. Before you go, run your VIN through nhtsa.gov/recalls - it will tell you whether your XT6 is genuinely affected and whether the cable replacement has already been done. Cadillac customer service is at 1-800-458-8006 if the dealer cannot help.

rows.title: Recall 22V446000: Fuel Tank Rollover Valve May Fail to Seal on 2022 XT6
rows.description: Certain 2022 Cadillac XT6 crossovers were recalled by General Motors for a fuel tank rollover valve that may not seal properly in a rollover crash. NHTSA files the defect against the gasoline storage tank assembly. The rollover valve's whole purpose is to shut the tank's vent path when the XT6 is no longer upright, keeping gasoline inside the tank rather than letting it run out through the vent. On the recalled vehicles the valve can be dislodged from its position or absent altogether, which leaves nothing to close that path. GM's stated consequence is direct: fuel can leak during a rollover crash, and that raises the risk of a fire. This is not a drivability problem — the XT6 runs and refuels normally with the defect present, which is exactly why it is worth confirming by VIN rather than waiting to notice something wrong.
rows.solution: Correction is free of charge at a Cadillac dealer under NHTSA campaign 22V446000, GM number N222366070. The dealer inspects the fuel tank and replaces the fuel tank shell if the rollover valve turns out to be dislodged or missing; if the valve is properly in place, no replacement is needed. Owner letters went out July 27, 2022. Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls to see whether the remedy has been performed, and call Cadillac customer service at 1-800-458-8006 with questions.

rows.title: 3.6L V6 Timing Chain Concern (XT6)
rows.description: The XT6 uses the GM 3.6L V6 (LGX) which has a documented history of timing chain stretch across the GM lineup. While the LGX generation is improved over earlier 3.6L variants, the three-chain design with plastic guides remains a long-term reliability concern. Most XT6s are still too new for widespread timing chain failures, but owners should monitor for early signs and plan for preventive replacement around 100,000-120,000 miles based on the engine's history in other models.
rows.solution: Monitor for timing chain rattle on cold starts. If codes or rattle develop, complete timing chain replacement is needed. Preventive replacement at 100,000-120,000 miles is wise based on the 3.6L's track record. Same Cloyes 9-0753S kit as other 3.6L applications.

rows.title: 9-Speed Automatic Transmission Shudder and Harsh Shifts
rows.description: The XT6's GM 9T65 9-speed automatic transmission exhibits shuddering during light throttle acceleration between 25-50 mph, similar to driving over rumble strips. The torque converter clutch wears prematurely, contaminating the transmission fluid.
rows.solution: A transmission fluid flush with the updated Mobil 1 Blue Label fluid resolves mild cases. Severe cases require torque converter replacement. A GM TSB authorizes fluid flush as the first repair attempt.

rows.title: Water Leaks Into the Interior Through Pinholes in the Roof Panel Laser Braze — Wet Carpet and Inoperative Liftgate Actuator
rows.description: GM bulletin 19-NA-167 covers water leaking into the interior on the 2020-2021 Cadillac XT6 (alongside the 2017-2021 XT5 and GMC Acadia). Owners find wet carpet or headliner at the front and/or rear, on either side, typically after rain or a car wash. The cause is not the sunroof drains that owners and shops usually chase first: it is pinhole voids in the laser braze joint between the roof panel and the outer body ring, and in the seam sealer over it. The bulletin says the pinholes are most often found near the top of the windshield at the A-pillars, or near the top of the liftgate at the D-pillars. Water entering at the D-pillars runs down into the rear of the vehicle, and the bulletin specifically notes that on the XT6 the liftgate actuator may become noisy or inoperative as a result — so an electrical complaint at the tailgate is a symptom of the body leak, not a separate failure. Left alone, trapped water rots carpet padding, grows mold, and corrodes rear body connectors.
rows.solution: Have the shop follow 19-NA-167 rather than starting with sunroof drain cleaning. The diagnosis is a water test of the roof-to-body laser braze at the A-pillar and D-pillar corners to find the pinholes, followed by resealing the braze joint and seam sealer at the void. Any water-damaged carpet and padding must be lifted and fully dried, and a liftgate actuator that has been soaked usually needs replacement even after the leak is sealed. Expect roughly $300-$1,200 for the leak repair and drying at a dealer, more if the actuator or a wet module has to be replaced; this is a factory body-sealing defect, so ask about warranty coverage before authorizing a paid repair.

rows.title: Windshield Not Properly Bonded to the Body — Missing Urethane Sealant, Recall 23V681
rows.description: NHTSA campaign 23V681000 covers 2024 Cadillac XT6 vehicles whose windshield may not have been bonded to the body with the proper urethane sealant during assembly. The windshield is a structural part of the vehicle: it braces the roof in a rollover and it provides the backstop the passenger airbag deploys against. A windshield that is not properly bonded can separate from the body in a crash, so the passenger airbag may not restrain the occupant as designed and the roof loses crush resistance. On the road, an unbonded windshield can also let water and wind noise in, or in the worst case detach at speed.
rows.solution: A free recall remedy exists. Dealers inspect the windshield bond, apply primer and urethane sealant where it is missing, or replace the windshield entirely if it is damaged during inspection — all at no charge, under NHTSA 23V681000. Owner notification began November 27, 2023. Do not have an unrepaired vehicle's windshield replaced by a third party before the recall inspection; the dealer repair is free and independent glass work can complicate the claim.

rows.title: 2.0L EcoBoost coolant loss / EGR cooler leak — low coolant, white smoke, overheat
rows.description: 2019-2020 Nautilus models with the base 2.0L EcoBoost (non-hybrid) suffer unexplained coolant loss, white tailpipe smoke, an overheat warning, and sometimes coolant intrusion into the cylinders. Ford TSB 20-2234 traces the most common cause to a failing exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) cooler that leaks coolant internally; the related design also has a known coolant-intrusion weakness (narrow coolant slit between cylinders compromising the head-gasket seal). Owners report repeated coolant top-offs with no visible external leak, then misfires as coolant fouls the plugs. A June 2025 Ford EcoBoost coolant-intrusion class action covers 1.5L-2.0L engines; the most severe Nautilus cases require engine replacement with the redesigned block.
rows.solution: Per TSB 20-2234, perform a cooling-system pressure test and inspect the EGR cooler; replace the EGR cooler and update PCM software for the typical case. If a coolant smell, white smoke, and cylinder misfires persist (coolant intrusion past the head gasket), the durable fix is a long-block / engine replacement with the updated cross-drilled block — a head-gasket-only repair on the old-style block will fail again. Replace fouled spark plugs and flush the cooling system.

rows.title: 2.7L EcoBoost cold-start VCT rattle (top-front-cover tick/tap on startup)
rows.description: Nautilus models with the optional 2.7L EcoBoost V6 produce a ticking, tapping, or rattle noise from the top-front-cover area of the engine on initial start-up after a cold soak of 6 hours or more, lasting roughly 2-5 seconds. Ford TSB 23-2356 (superseding 22-2376 and 23-2049) attributes the noise to stuck internal components in the variable cam timing (VCT) / cam phaser units. Left unaddressed it can set crank/cam correlation codes (P0016). It is a well-documented EcoBoost cam-phaser pattern failure also seen on the F-150 2.7L.
rows.solution: Per TSB 23-2356 the prescribed repair is to replace all four VCT (cam phaser) units — a substantial ~14.7-hour labor job. Using the correct oil viscosity and avoiding extended oil-change intervals helps slow phaser wear. Many out-of-warranty owners report Ford goodwill covering a large portion (one owner quoted ~$2,600 with ~2/3 covered at 88k miles).

rows.title: 8F35 8-speed automatic shudder, buck, and jerk under 35 mph
rows.description: Nautilus models built on or before March 11, 2021 with the 8F35 8-speed automatic commonly exhibit a shudder, buck, hesitation, or jerk while accelerating from a stop up to about 35 mph (57 km/h). Ford Technical Service Bulletin 21-2389 (superseding 21-2081) attributes the condition primarily to PCM/transmission solenoid control software rather than internal mechanical wear, though severe untreated cases progressed to harsh shifting and, in a minority of CarComplaints reports, complete transmission failure. This is the single most-complained-about Nautilus problem and is the subject of a Chimicles Schwartz Kriner class-action investigation covering 2019-2021 Edge/Nautilus 8F35 vehicles.
rows.solution: First-line fix per TSB 21-2389 is to reprogram the PCM with the latest software level and update the transmission solenoid (adaptive) strategy (about 0.9 hours labor, typically covered under the 6yr/70k powertrain warranty). If the shudder persists after reprogramming, the shop should inspect for a failing torque converter, worn clutch packs, or contaminated fluid and replace as needed. A transmission fluid service with the correct Mercon ULV is recommended at the same time.

rows.title: Auto Start-Stop malfunction / engine won't auto-restart (weak 12V battery)
rows.description: Nautilus owners frequently report the Auto Start-Stop system behaving erratically — failing to engage, failing to auto-restart smoothly at the light, or throwing a system-fault/malfunction message. The most common root cause is the 12V battery state-of-charge falling below the threshold the system needs (the AGM start-stop battery degrades faster than a conventional battery), so the system disables itself or restarts roughly. The popularity of plug-and-play 'start-stop eliminator' modules for the Nautilus reflects how much the behavior annoys owners.
rows.solution: Test the 12V battery and charging system; replace a weak or aged AGM battery with the correct spec and perform a Battery Monitoring System (BMS) reset so the PCM relearns state-of-charge. Ensure parasitic-draw and software are current. Owners who simply dislike the feature use the dash defeat button each drive or a plug-and-play disable module (not a repair, a preference).

rows.title: Panoramic Vista Roof water leaks from clogged sunroof drains
rows.description: Nautilus models equipped with the panoramic Vista Roof commonly develop water leaks traced to clogged or failing sunroof drain tubes and a sunroof track/seal design that was revised after the 2020 model year. Owners report water dripping over the dash after rain, water pooling in the rear cargo/spare-tire well, soaked rear floorboards and insulation, and musty smells. Severe, unresolved cases (one 2020 with nine shop visits) escalated to Lemon Law claims. The water can also reach electrical modules, contributing to secondary faults.
rows.solution: Have the dealer clear/flush the four sunroof drain tubes (they route from the roof corners down the A- and C-pillars) and verify outlets are not pinched or disconnected. Inspect and reseal/replace the sunroof track and seals; dry out and replace water-damaged carpet/insulation to prevent mold and corrosion. Repairs are covered under the 4yr/50k bumper-to-bumper warranty when in period.

rows.title: Power liftgate inoperative / opens or closes on its own (RGTM software, motor, strut)
rows.description: The hands-free power liftgate frequently becomes intermittent or fully inoperative on first-generation (2019-2023) Nautilus. The system uses a single electric motor on the driver's side plus a gas strut on the passenger side; failures include the motor straining without the latch releasing, the gate not responding to the fob/dash button/kick sensor, and the gate opening or closing on its own while parked. Ford documents that many 2019-2020 cases are Rear Gate Trunk Module (RGTM) software, while others are a weak motor or a worn gas support strut (one owner quoted ~$1,200 for struts).
rows.solution: Start with an RGTM software reprogram and a power-liftgate re-initialization procedure, which resolves many no-open/erratic cases without parts. If the gate is mechanically weak or won't hold position, replace the failing gas support strut and/or the liftgate drive motor. Verify the kick-sensor and latch operation after repair.

rows.title: Rearview Camera Software Error — Blank Image or Image That Won't Clear (Recall 25S72 / NHTSA 25V442)
rows.description: 2019 and 2020 Lincoln Nautilus crossovers are covered by NHTSA recall 25V442000, Ford's campaign 25S72, for a rearview camera software defect. The fault has two possible presentations: the camera can show a blank image instead of the view behind the vehicle, or the rearview image can remain on the center display even after the driver has finished backing and shifted out of reverse. Ford describes the safety consequence directly — a blank image reduces the driver's view behind the Nautilus, and a stale image left on screen can distract the driver — and says either can increase the risk of a crash. Note that this is a separate action from the earlier Nautilus backup-camera recall; if your VIN shows 25V442000 open, that campaign has its own remedy regardless of any camera work done previously.
rows.solution: Take the Nautilus to a Lincoln dealer for a free rearview camera software update. There is no cost to the owner and no part to buy. Owner notification letters went out September 4, 2025. To confirm whether your specific vehicle still needs the update — especially if the SUV was bought used or has had prior camera-related recall work — run the VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls and look for campaign 25V442000. Ford's customer line is 1-866-436-7332 and the internal reference is 25S72.

rows.title: SYNC 3 / APIM infotainment freezes, black-screens, and reboots
rows.description: First-generation Nautilus owners widely report the SYNC 3 center touchscreen freezing, going completely black, or spontaneously rebooting while driving — sometimes leaving only the backup camera working. Symptoms point to memory corruption in the APIM (Accessory Protocol Interface Module / SYNC module) software rather than the display panel itself, so a black or frozen screen usually traces to the APIM. Distinct from the 2024+ panoramic/center-display reboot recall (25V337), which is the newer multimedia module on the redesigned model.
rows.solution: Try a SYNC master reset (hold the power/volume button and Seek-Right for 10 seconds) and install the latest SYNC 3 software via USB or OTA. If freezes recur, the APIM module is reprogrammed or replaced by the dealer; updating to the current software level resolves most memory-related lockups. A pending USB drive update can also stop the reboot loop.

rows.title: Weak A/C Performance in Hot Weather
rows.description: The Nissan Kicks has widespread complaints about weak air conditioning performance, especially in temperatures above 90F. The undersized A/C system struggles to cool the cabin adequately. Nissan issued TSB NTB19-041 addressing A/C performance concerns. The issue is partially due to the small compressor paired with the 1.6L engine.
rows.solution: Verify refrigerant charge is correct (do not overfill). Check A/C condenser for debris blocking airflow. Dealer may apply TSB NTB19-041 software update to optimize compressor operation. Some owners add tinted windows or a cabin air recirculation fix to improve cooling.

rows.title: Blank / Partial Instrument Cluster on Cold Start (Combination Meter Recall 26V331)
rows.description: NHTSA recall 26V331 and Nissan campaign PMA66 apply to 51,598 model-year 2025-2026 Kicks vehicles produced June 24, 2024 through January 9, 2026. A combination-meter software logic error can cause communication loss between the graphic controller and automotive controller during cold start, producing a partial, blue or blank display and hiding required telltales and indicators. Nissan reported seven technical reports and 205 warranty claims, not owner-report totals.
rows.solution: Check the VIN for 26V331/PMA66. Nissan dealers update the combination-meter software with CONSULT 4 at no charge; the Part 573 report estimates about 0.5 hour and lists July 1, 2026 as the planned owner-notification date. Do not buy a cluster, display, controller, wiring harness or software product from this page; recall eligibility and the official software remedy must be confirmed first.

rows.title: Center Display Goes Blank in Reverse — No Backup Camera Image (Recall 25V324)
rows.description: NHTSA recall 25V324 covers certain 2025 Kicks and Frontier vehicles with an affected Center Information Display. A software logic error can cause a communication error with the In-Vehicle Infotainment module, leaving the rearview monitor blank in reverse and reducing rearward visibility. The combined population is 79,755 vehicles; the exact Kicks production window is June 24, 2024 through March 7, 2025, and eligibility remains VIN-specific.
rows.solution: Check the VIN for 25V324/PMA48. Nissan dealers update the Center Information Display software through CONSULT 3+ and a Nissan-provided jumper harness at no charge; the Part 573 report lists July 1, 2025 as the planned owner-notification date. Do not buy a camera, Center Information Display, IVI module, harness or software product from this page; recall eligibility and the official software remedy must be confirmed first.

rows.title: CVT Drone and Noise at Highway Speeds
rows.description: The Kicks' CVT produces excessive drone and noise at highway speeds (60-75 MPH). The CVT holds high RPMs (3,500-4,000) for highway cruising due to the small 1.6L engine's limited torque, creating a constant loud droning noise in the cabin. This is partly a design characteristic of the powertrain but is significantly louder than competitors. Sound deadening in the Kicks is minimal.
rows.solution: This is largely a design characteristic that cannot be fully eliminated. Aftermarket sound deadening material (Dynamat or similar) applied to the doors, floor, and firewall can reduce interior noise by 3-5 dB ($200-$500 DIY). Higher-quality tires designed for low road noise (Michelin Defender, Continental TrueContact) also help. Some owners report slightly lower RPMs and noise after a CVT fluid change.

rows.title: CVT Overheating During Highway Driving
rows.description: The Nissan Kicks CVT transmission (Jatco CVT7 W/R) overheats during sustained highway driving, particularly in hot weather or hilly terrain. The transmission enters limp mode to protect itself, limiting speed to 40-50 mph. The small displacement 1.6L engine forces the CVT to work harder at highway speeds, contributing to heat buildup.
rows.solution: Ensure CVT fluid is fresh with Nissan NS-3 (change every 30,000 miles). Avoid sustained high-speed driving in extreme heat. Some owners install auxiliary transmission coolers ($150-300 DIY). If overheating is chronic, TCM software update may be available at dealer.

rows.title: Door Retention Defect: Striker Weld Can Fail (Recall 26V023000)
rows.description: The 2026 Kicks is included in a Nissan safety recall covering improperly welded door strikers. The striker is the part mounted to the body that the door latch closes around, so when a poorly welded striker breaks, the door loses its retention and can open while the Kicks is being driven — which Nissan flags as an increased risk of injury or a crash. The defect puts the vehicles out of compliance with Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard 206 on door locks and door retention components. The 26,432-unit figure NHTSA publishes is the size of the entire campaign across all included Nissan models; it says nothing about how many Kicks are affected. Nissan's campaign numbers are PD185 and PMA61.
rows.solution: Nissan dealers will replace the door strikers free of charge. Notification letters went out to owners on March 17, 2026, and affected VINs have been searchable through NHTSA since January 28, 2026. Check your 2026 Kicks by VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls; if it comes back as affected, book the striker replacement at a Nissan dealer. For help, Nissan customer service is at 800-647-7261 — quote recall PD185/PMA61.

rows.title: Electric Power Steering (EPS) Assist Loss — Torque Sensor Weld Failure (Recall PMA25/PMA26)
rows.description: Certain 2021 Kicks (built July 19-September 27, 2021) have an intermittent electrical connection in the electric power steering torque sensor caused by poor weld penetration at a terminal that can disconnect. When it fails, EPS assist is disabled, a warning light illuminates, and steering reverts to much heavier manual effort, increasing crash risk. Nissan recalled 2021 Kicks and Versa vehicles after investigating loss-of-assist incidents.
rows.solution: Recall remedy PMA25/PMA26: Nissan dealers inspect the steering column torque sensor lot code and replace the steering column assembly if an affected lot is found, free of charge. Verify the VIN against the recall at a Nissan dealer or nhtsa.gov.

rows.title: Excessive Engine Noise and Vibration (HR16DE)
rows.description: The Kicks HR16DE 1.6L engine produces excessive noise and vibration that transmits into the cabin, particularly at highway RPMs where the CVT holds the engine at 3,000-4,000 RPM. The lack of sound insulation and the CVT's tendency to keep RPMs high under load amplifies the issue.
rows.solution: Check engine and transmission mounts for wear. Add sound deadening material to firewall and floor ($100-300 DIY). Some owners report improvement after dealer applies ECM calibration update that adjusts CVT shift points to lower cruising RPM.

rows.title: Engine Stalling / Shutting Off While Driving (Throttle Body, MAF Sensor, ECM Software)
rows.description: Many 2018-2020 Kicks owners report the engine stalling or shutting off, often when slowing to a stop and in some cases at speed, sometimes with a delayed restart. Dealers and forums commonly trace it to the throttle body, a contaminated mass airflow (MAF) sensor, or outdated ECM software; throttle-body replacement and ECM reprogramming have resolved repeat cases. RepairPal documents engine-stalling as a recognized Kicks complaint, frequently alongside DTC P0101.
rows.solution: Have the dealer scan for stored codes (commonly P0101) and check for applicable ECM reprogramming before replacing parts. Common fixes include cleaning or replacing the MAF sensor, replacing the throttle body and gasket, and applying the latest ECM software update.

rows.title: Infotainment Touchscreen Freezing / Rebooting and CarPlay Disconnects
rows.description: Kicks owners report the infotainment touchscreen freezing or becoming unresponsive (requiring a restart), the system randomly rebooting on its own, and frequent Apple CarPlay / Android Auto disconnections, failures to connect, or audio that cuts out after a few minutes. The failures are predominantly software-related rather than hardware faults, and a dealer software update (TSB NTB23-018) addresses many cases.
rows.solution: Try a certified USB data cable, inspect the USB port for debris, and restart both the phone and the head unit (hold the power/volume knob ~10-20 seconds); ensure phone OS and vehicle infotainment firmware are current. If freezing or random reboots persist, have a Nissan dealer apply the latest infotainment/audio firmware update (per TSB) or diagnose the head unit.

rows.title: Rear Drum Brake Squeal and Dust Contamination
rows.description: The Kicks uses rear drum brakes (a cost-saving measure) that develop squealing, grinding, and poor performance from brake dust accumulation. The semi-sealed drum design traps dust and debris, causing noise and inconsistent braking. The issue is worse in dusty or wet environments. The drums also warp easily, causing a pulsation felt through the brake pedal.
rows.solution: Remove rear drums and clean all components with brake cleaner. Inspect shoes for glazing and contamination — sand the shoe surface lightly with 120-grit sandpaper if glazed. Check drums for scoring and measure for out-of-round (max 0.006"). Replace shoes and drums if worn. Apply brake grease to the backing plate contact points. Clean rear brakes every 20,000 miles as preventive maintenance.

rows.title: Rearview Camera Image Disappears / Stays Off (AV Control Unit Recall 19V654)
rows.description: NHTSA recall 19V654 and Nissan campaign R1911 apply to certain 2018-2019 Kicks vehicles. The AV control-unit software can retain a driver-adjusted display setting that prevents the rearview image from returning at the start of a later reverse event, failing the rear-visibility requirement. Eligibility is VIN-specific within a broader Nissan and Infiniti population.
rows.solution: Check the VIN for 19V654/R1911. Nissan dealers reprogram the AV control unit so the rearview image returns at the beginning of each backing event at no charge; the campaign bulletin lists a 0.2-hour operation. Do not buy a camera, AV control unit, display, wiring harness or software product from this page; recall eligibility and the official reprogramming remedy must be confirmed first.

rows.title: Automatic Emergency Braking / Forward Collision Phantom Activation
rows.description: Third-generation Muranos with Nissan's Forward Emergency Braking (FEB)/Automatic Emergency Braking (AEB) have widely reported 'phantom braking' — the system suddenly and forcefully brakes when no obstacle is present, creating rear-end collision and loss-of-control risk. The problem is associated with the front grille radar/sensor module (Bosch-supplied) misreading the road. The Murano is named in AEB class-action litigation alongside other Nissan models, and Nissan issued TSBs addressing false AEB/FCW activation on 2019-2024 Murano (Z52).
rows.solution: Dealer diagnosis per the applicable TSB; remedies have included radar sensor recalibration, software/ECU reprogramming, or sensor replacement. Keep the front emblem/grille radar area clean and free of obstructions (snow, mud, badges). The FEB system can be temporarily disabled via the vehicle settings menu while driving in conditions that trigger false activation.

rows.title: Battery Drain and No-Start from Telematics/Infotainment Modules Staying Awake
rows.description: A recurring owner complaint on newer Nissan crossovers, including Murano, is a dead battery after sitting overnight or for a few days despite the battery testing good initially. Reports often point to parasitic draw from telematics, AV control, or body control modules that fail to enter sleep mode, sometimes accompanied by app connectivity glitches or infotainment oddities. The issue can be intermittent, making it difficult to catch unless a proper draw test is performed after module timeout.
rows.solution: Start with battery state-of-health and charging-system checks, then perform a parasitic draw test with the vehicle fully asleep. If draw remains excessive, isolate the circuit by pulling fuses and checking telematics, AV, and BCM-related branches; software updates, module resets, or replacement of the offending module may be required. Replacing the battery alone often provides only temporary relief if the root draw remains.

rows.title: Front Driver Seat Frame/Track Looseness Causing Rocking, Clicking, or Unintended Movement
rows.description: Owners have reported the driver's seat rocking front-to-back, clicking during braking/acceleration, or feeling loose on its track. Nissan has issued service information on seat track/frame-related movement complaints on late-model vehicles, and owner reports indicate the issue can appear at relatively low mileage. The problem is usually caused by play in the seat track assembly, frame hardware, or worn internal seat adjuster components rather than the floor mounting points themselves.
rows.solution: Road-test the vehicle and confirm whether the movement occurs during throttle tip-in, braking, or over bumps. Inspect seat track bolts, rail alignment, and the seat adjuster assembly; repairs typically involve tightening hardware to spec, replacing the seat track/adjuster assembly, or replacing the seat frame if internal play is present. If the seat has power functions, verify all positions after repair and recalibrate memory settings if equipped.

rows.title: Front Radar/Sensor Malfunctions Triggering AEB, ICC, and Forward Collision Warnings
rows.description: Nissan NTB19-033G applies to 2015-2024 Murano Z52 vehicles when ICC stops working, the AEB/FEB warning illuminates, or a front-radar obstruction message appears and C1A16, C1A16-97, C2582 or C2582-97 is the only stored DTC. Its flow separates obstruction and weather from repeat incidents, sensor manufacture date, replacement where authorized and required sensor alignment. The frozen 2021-2024 page is inside that exact boundary.
rows.solution: Preserve all DTCs and confirm whether obstruction or severe weather explains the event. Use NTB19-033G only when one listed radar DTC is the sole stored code; the bulletin repeatedly says not to replace the distance sensor outside its flow. When replacement is authorized, use the EPC for the VIN-specific sensor and perform alignment. Do not buy a radar sensor or bracket from this page; DTC state, manufacture date, diagnosis, calibration and VIN fitment must be established first.

rows.title: Rearview Camera Image Blank, Distorted, or Intermittent Due to AV Control Unit/Camera Fault
rows.description: Multiple Murano owners in the 2021-2024 range have reported the backup camera showing a black screen, frozen image, blue screen, or distorted picture when shifting into reverse. This is also covered by Nissan/NHTSA recall actions affecting rearview camera display reliability on Nissan vehicles, including Murano, because the image may not display as required by FMVSS 111. Owners typically experience intermittent failure at first, then more frequent loss of image, especially after startup or in hot/cold weather.
rows.solution: Confirm the concern by repeatedly cycling ignition and selecting reverse while monitoring the display. Diagnosis usually involves checking for AV control unit software/hardware faults, camera harness connection issues, and camera module failure; Nissan recall/TSB procedures generally call for software update, AV control unit reprogramming, or replacement of the camera/control unit if the image remains unstable. If the vehicle is covered by an open recall, the recall remedy should be completed before paid repairs.

rows.title: Sunroof Drain or Roof Area Water Intrusion Causing Wet Headliner/Carpet and Electrical Issues
rows.description: Murano owners continue to report water leaks into the cabin, often showing up as damp headliner edges, wet front footwells, musty odor, or water near A-pillars after rain or car washes. The most common causes are restricted sunroof drains, disconnected drain tubes, or seal/body seam issues around the roof opening area. If ignored, the leak can damage carpet padding, connectors, and interior electronics.
rows.solution: Water-test the roof and windshield perimeter while inspecting the sunroof cassette drains and A-pillar drain routing. Clear clogged drains with low-pressure air or line, repair or reconnect drain tubes, and inspect for seal or seam leaks if drains flow normally. Dry the carpet and underlayment thoroughly afterward to prevent mold and corrosion in connectors under the carpet.
